can i stop it scanning every stock or reading the news

Yes, both are in Setup → Settings. Scan all US stocks every day → Off (only the watchlist) makes the swing desk pick only from its watchlist. Let Kestrel read the news → Off stops the headlines. With news on, it reads Alpaca's feed (Benzinga) with your keys, or Yahoo's without, shows headlines next to stocks, and won't buy a stock with danger headlines in the last 3 days, like a share offering, bankruptcy or trading halt. News never makes it buy. Press Save settings after changing either.

does it ever use margin or borrow money?

Never. It spends only cash. When it reads your balance it uses cash you can trade with, not borrowed buying power; at Alpaca it takes the smaller of cash and non-marginable buying power. Every Alpaca account is technically a margin type (Alpaca has no cash accounts), but under $2,000 it can't borrow, and Kestrel never borrows either way. At Schwab and Webull it follows cash-account rules by default and spends settled money only.

how do i connect my schwab account

Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Charles Schwab. From developer.schwab.com, paste your app's App Key, Secret and Callback address exactly as registered (for example https://127.0.0.1:8182, no slash at the end); add the account number only if you have several. Press Save Schwab keys, then Open Schwab login, sign in and approve. Your browser ends on a page that won't load; that's expected. Paste that page's whole address into The address you landed on, press Finish login, then Test Schwab. Log in about once a week: Schwab's limit is 7 days.

so what does this app actually do, does it trade for me automatically

Yes, once the autopilot is on, but in stages. First it studies and practices with pretend money. In Setup, the Start Stage 1 paper trading button lets the swing desk paper trade the momentum method right away; it decides 15 minutes before each close. Real money only comes after at least 30 trading days of paper results that pass your rules (made money, beat the S&P 500, never dropped more than 10% from its best day), plus a typed confirmation in the full Setup menu. The window shows your account against the S&P 500, positions, every trade and why, and has Pause and Emergency stop buttons.

why compare tjr with random trades

Because a stop and a 2-to-1 target can look profitable on their own. The placebo buys at random moments in the same 9:35-11:30am window, with the same trend filter, stop and target, so if TJR's setup can't beat it per trade, the setup itself isn't adding anything. That was a real concern: in the 16-year daily test, TJR longs averaged +0.24R per trade, but random entries with the same stop and target got +0.18R.

why doesn't kestrel short stocks?

Kestrel only buys; there's no short selling in it, and its hard rules say it spends only cash and never borrows. The evidence so far doesn't argue for adding it: in the 16-year daily test, TJR's short setups lost in every version (about −0.24R per trade, profit factor 0.66-0.68). The real-money plan is also small ($50), and at Alpaca an account under $2,000 can't borrow anyway. Schwab and Webull run under cash-account rules, spending settled money only.

what's danger news

When news is on, the bot reads recent headlines (the last 3 days) from Alpaca's news feed, or Yahoo without keys. If a stock's headlines contain words like offering, bankrupt, chapter 11, trading halt, delist, going concern, SEC charges, fraud, reverse split, default, restatement or subpoena, it won't buy that stock for now. Stocks in play with danger news are skipped too. News never makes it buy anything; it only keeps it away.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

how do i stop everything right now?

Use the emergency stop. In the app, press Emergency stop and type SELL EVERYTHING. From Telegram, send /kill SELL EVERYTHING (exactly that phrase). In Terminal, run `python run.py kill`. It cancels the bot's own orders, sells everything the bot owns with market orders, and halts both desks. It never sells your own stocks. If a sale doesn't go through, it keeps trying every 5 minutes, and you can also sell at the broker yourself.

does paper trading follow the settlement rules too?

Yes. Paper trading uses the same cash-account setting as your real-money broker, so if real money would go to a cash account, paper also spends settled money only. That way the paper results match what real money would do. The simulated paper broker on your Mac also fills every order 0.05% worse than the quoted price, because real orders rarely fill at exactly the price you saw.

what am i looking at on the summary tab

Summary is the overview. On top: a Right now line saying what the autopilot and each desk are doing, the account picker, the account value and today's change, and tiles for Cash, Total return, Worst drop from peak and Win rate. Then a chart of your account against the S&P 500 from the same starting amount (ranges 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y, All; hover or use the arrow keys, or press Table for the numbers), the Desks card with each desk's step (Study, Plan, Paper, Live), a Positions preview, and the Watchlist.

what happens if the account drops a lot

There are layers. Each position has a stop-loss: 7% on the swing desk, 1-5% sized to the stock on the day desk. If a desk is down more than 3% on the day, it stops buying for that day. If it falls 15% below its best point, the kill switch sells everything that desk owns and halts it, and a real-money desk drops back to paper. Separately, a desk can't go live at all if its paper trading ever dropped more than 10% from its best day.

i have about 5k sitting in my schwab account, will the bot use all of it?

No. It only uses up to the real-money cap you set in Setup (your plan is $50), whatever else is in the account. Its checkbook only holds the money and positions it opened itself, so it never touches your other cash or stocks. Before buying it also checks the cash the broker says is available and spends the smaller amount. Kestrel treats Schwab as a cash account, so it only spends settled money there.

calendar has finished trades and account value buttons, whats the difference

Finished trades, the default, counts only money made or lost on trades that closed that day, so a day without finished trades stays blank. Account value shows the whole account's change that day, which includes the moves of stocks it still holds. So a day can show a loss in Account value with no trades at all, because something it owns dropped. The week totals and the month line follow whichever one you pick.

why is my strategy on half size

Because it's been losing so far. Once a strategy has at least 12 finished trades in that account and its average result is below zero, the bot halves its maximum position size: on the swing desk, 12.5% becomes 6.25% of the desk. It's re-checked after every trade, so once the average turns positive it goes back to normal. If it keeps losing clearly over 30+ trades, it gets paused instead.

why is the calendar blue and red instead of green

Blue means a gain and red a loss, a pair that stays readable with color-blindness. Every day also shows its amount with a plus or minus sign, so you never have to rely on color alone. A deeper shade means a bigger day compared with the rest of that month. The legend under the calendar labels them Made money and Lost money.

does kestrel update itself or do i have to download every new version

It updates itself. While the app is open (it can sit minimized), it checks its download page when it opens and once a day. When there's a newer version it downloads it, checks the download's fingerprint and signature, swaps itself and restarts, and a running background autopilot restarts on the new version. With paper trading only, this happens automatically. If real money is involved, it asks you first. It must be in your Applications folder to replace itself. Versions before 1.0.13 can't update themselves: download the zip once more by hand.

does kestrel auto-update while it's trading real money?

No, it asks first. With paper trading only, it updates by itself. If real money is involved, meaning LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, a desk trading real money, or real shares or orders still open, it asks you before installing, so new code never takes over real money unannounced. If it can't confirm that no real money is involved, it treats that as "ask first" too. Turning off Update Automatically in the Kestrel menu makes it always ask. Your keys and data stay either way.

can i close my laptop and still have it trade

Yes, if it's plugged in and you turn on Setup → 2. Autopilot → Keep trading with the lid closed. Then the Mac stays awake with the lid closed and keeps trading. On battery it sleeps as usual, so unplugged with the lid shut, it isn't trading. Other options: keep the lid open with the charger in, or use clamshell mode (lid closed with an external monitor and power). Lid-closed mode also sets a weekday 8:30am wake-up, but wake-ups with the lid closed aren't guaranteed, so plugged in and awake is the dependable setup.

what's the difference between webull paper keys and real money keys?

They're separate keys for separate servers: Webull's paper (test) keys only work on its test server, and real-money keys only on its real server. Setup asks which kind you pasted, and if you pick wrong, Test Webull finds out and switches. Paper trading at Webull needs the paper keys and Paper trading happens at: Webull. Real money at Webull needs real-money keys, Broker for real money: Webull, and the same locks as elsewhere: passing paper results, LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true and your typed REAL MONEY.

when does the after market report come out and where do i find it

About 25 minutes after each close (New York time), as long as the autopilot is on. It's at the top of the Journal tab under After-market report, with a date picker for the last week. It's also saved on your Mac in ~/AITrader/data/reports/ as after-market-<date>.md, and python run.py report prints it. If Telegram is paired, you get the whole report there; with Pushover you get its summary. Telegram's /report command sends it on request.

what time does the day desk stop trading

On a normal day the market closes at 4:00pm New York time. The day desk opens no new trades from 3:30pm (30 minutes before the close) and sells everything at 3:50pm (10 minutes before). On early-close days, when the market shuts at 1:00pm, those become 12:30pm and 12:50pm. Stop-losses keep working right up to the sell-off.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.
